values: Synthetic lifestyle and skin dryness dataset: EDA

Interpretation: the designed rules should show 1–3 dryness when sleep and water are adequate, 4–6 when water is low despite adequate sleep, and 7–10 when both are low. This is synthetic data for prototyping, not a clinical prediction model.
All records use oily to model the requested persona.
Whole-hour part of the sleep duration.
Remaining-minute part; combine with hours for calculations.
Synthetic self-reported desire for water, increased by water shortfall, short sleep and outdoor band.
Readable label for the four user choices.
Representative minute value inside the selected choice. No values are generated for 121–179 minutes because the supplied choices omit 2–3 hours.
Synthetic model target; not a clinical diagnostic score.
low: 0–3; moderate: 4–6; high: 7–10 for prototype display.
Synthetic self-reported oiliness for an oily-skin baseline.
normal, mildly_dry, dry, very_dry, or oily_dehydrated.
Primary synthetic calibration: adequate sleep + adequate water → dryness 1–3; adequate sleep + low water → 4–6; low sleep + low water → 7–10.
Evidence about increased fluid intake and skin hydration is limited/weak overall; used only as directional context, not to set clinical thresholds.
Poor sleep quality was associated with diminished skin-barrier recovery in a small observational study; used as directional context for the sleep feature.
UV exposure can affect epidermal barrier function; outdoor choice is retained as a weak proxy only, not a measure of UV dose or sunscreen use.
Provides broad total-water context. It includes water from food and beverages, so it is not used as a personal drinking-water prescription or a model label.
This dataset is simulated for prototype/EDA work. It must not be presented as clinical evidence, used for medical decisions, or described as Zepp/Amazfit output.
